work_candidate.original_synopsis: Responding to a decades-old distress call, the da Vinci locates an inhabited station precariously anchored near a black hole called Demon. Its Resaurian occupants initially threaten a Starfleet away team, then disclose that the facility was used to imprison political opponents, contradicting a visiting councilman's account of an abandoned research station. Gomez and her engineers find that the station's gravity shielding and time-dilation behavior do not match all resident explanations. As Tev designs a tractor-assisted extraction, he suspects interference from a Resaurian ship but has not proved sabotage. The anchor fails and the station plunges toward the event horizon while crew members are injured or incapacitated. Gold orders the da Vinci into the black hole's vicinity to attempt a rescue. The source stops on a cliffhanger; whether any rescue succeeds is not established in Book One.

chapter_spans.original_summary: Resaurian Captain S'linth makes a ritual offering near Demon, hears an anomalous signal and privately believes he recognizes its source while Suliss fears the implications.
Gomez and Tev reconstruct a degraded subspace distress transmission, exposing working-style friction and establishing a distant emergency rather than an identified sender.
Gold wakes from an alarming dream about his granddaughter and reflects on his replacement hand; the ship sets course toward the unresolved call near Resaurian space.
A gravity anomaly halts warp, and Tev's observations allow Gomez to infer that the signal originates near a black hole.
Probe relays reveal a seemingly anchored station inside the photon sphere; shields and exceptional gravity block straightforward transporter and life-sign checks.
Another visitor's ion trail cannot establish its fate. Tev manages a relay as the away team beams to the station, loses contact and meets armed residents.
S'linth wants open contact but Sha'a urges delay; Gold hails the Dutiful Burden while Tev traces the missing away team.
Konya senses fear and anger and intervenes to prevent the station guards from firing. First contact de-escalates without confirmation of renewed ship communications.
Councilman Sha'a claims the site was a research outpost abandoned after an insanity plague; Gold doubts the account, and historical records are incomplete.
S'eth reports many surviving inhabitants and shield machinery tied to the station's anchor; he acknowledges original confinement but withholds key history.
Abramowitz and Soloman use damaged archival fragments to propose, not prove, a political cycle following Klingon withdrawal and a traditionalist reaction.
S'eth describes a political exile and an alleged eightfold time ratio, but limited food capacity and retained weapons challenge parts of his account.
Gold accuses Sha'a of maintaining a prison and demands rescue access. Sha'a denies killing detainees, while S'linth reacts as if new information alarms him.
Communications return; crew measurements suggest roughly twofold rather than eightfold time dilation. Tev sets up a tentative tractor-probe extraction plan.
Tev detects a competing Resaurian tractor beam and suspects deliberate disruption. The station falls inward, injuries follow, and Gold orders a risky rescue attempt before the continuation marker.

evidence.observation: S'linth hears an odd repeated signal during a ritual; his sense of recognition is his private interpretation, not verified signal provenance.
Gomez and Tev reconstruct a degraded signal described as approximately 93 years old; the recovered call signals distress but lacks an authenticated sender.
Gold's fear for his granddaughter appears within a nightmare and his reflections; it supplies no evidence that she was harmed.
Gomez and Tev associate their warp disruption and unusual gravity with a black hole; this is an in-story measurement-based inference.
Remote probes image a station within the photon sphere; unusual shields prevent reliable life-sign readings or a simple transporter solution.
An ion trail indicates a prior craft but cannot determine whether it escaped or fell inward; the away team loses communications after arrival.
S'linth proposes contact, Sha'a asks him to delay and Gold hails the Dutiful Burden; their motives remain differentiated from their speech.
Konya reports sensing fear and anger and stops guards from firing; his mental impression is not independent access to their motives.
Sha'a claims a research facility was abandoned due to an insanity plague; the claim is disputed and not established by an independent full history.
S'eth describes political prisoners and claims eightfold time dilation; provisioning and arms observations leave the account incomplete.
Crew tests put the ratio closer to twofold than S'eth's eightfold figure; measurement is provisional and conditions may vary.
Tev detects a competing tractor beam from the Resaurian ship and suspects an intentional anchor disruption; sabotage is not forensically verified.
The station loses its anchoring, people are injured, and Gold orders da Vinci toward the event horizon; the text ends before a rescue outcome.
